issue.title: gateway: the last candidate's stream error event saying too long reaches the agent raw, not as context_length_exceeded
issue.body:
Found while fixing ergou0954_54426's "Context window is full" (Discord #feedback, 2026-11-01).

When the **last** candidate left (a lone provider, or the last member of a group) answers HTTP 200 `text/event-stream` whose first event is an error that says the conversation is too long, the gateway passes the event through as the vendor wrote it. The agent never gets `context_length_exceeded` / "prompt is too long", so it doesn't compact.

Probe (chat protocol, scripted upstream answering `data: {"error":{"message":"Context window is full. Reduce conversation history, system prompt, or tools. (request id: 1)","type":"invalid_request_error"}}`), with and without `"stream":true`:

- `r/m` alone: 200, the raw error event, asked once.
- group of two, both answering that: the first is skipped as an overflow (failOverflow, no rest), the second's raw event reaches the agent as 200.

The same request answered with a 400 status gets `context_length_exceeded` (writeErrorSaid). Candidates that aren't last are fine: their stream is held and `streamStatus` reads the event as a 400 overflow.

This isn't specific to that wording: any tooLong text in the last candidate's stream error event passes through. The relays seen so far (kiro.rs, kiro2claude) send that text as a 400 before the stream starts, so the reporter's case is covered by the status path.

comments.body:
A fix is on [the fork branch](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/4675-last-stream-context-overflow), commit [b8b3eced8](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/b8b3eced8ffbeb8b7feb1be7d7a459d6962ccd51), based on `ed0ab567`.

For the last unheld SSE candidate, the gateway now examines the first complete event before sending it. A context overflow goes through the existing error mapping for the caller's protocol; other first events pass through immediately, and an error after content has begun stays in that stream. It does not buffer the whole successful reply. An incomplete first event beyond the existing `holdMost` limit passes through unchanged.

Real local HTTP gateway tests with fake upstreams reproduce the raw 200 overflow on the base for Chat, Messages and Responses, streamed and nonstreamed; those cases now pass, including a two-provider group and no account rest. The original red group had one member; the final two-member control was not separately captured red. Channel-controlled tests verify that content and an upstream heartbeat reach the client before the upstream ends, and that other errors, a partial event at EOF and an empty stream retain their old behavior. Parent related stream/overflow/refusal checks and final controls passed under `-race`; gateway vet, formatting and full `nogui` build passed. No real provider, full suite or cross-platform runtime was run. AI-assisted implementation and review.
